messages:
Taylor W: hey all, onboarding question: i'm on day 3 and need to run a quick streaming smoke test. i'm behind corp firewall. should i use sandbox or hosted key for local dev? and can security whitelist a stable IP for our test VM?

Nina (DevEx): welcome! use a sandbox key for local/dev tests. hosted keys = staging/prod. grab sandbox from Console -> API Keys. note sandbox has stricter quotas.

InfraBot: sandbox defaults: 55 req/min and 5 concurrent streaming connections per key. For temporary higher load, open an infra ticket with test window and expected qps.

Taylor W: got it. is there an easy way to make traffic originate from a stable IP so security can whitelist?

Omar - SRE: two options: 1) request access to the org devproxy which egresses from 52.15.90.10 (temporary whitelist ok), or 2) spin a test VM in our dev VPC and run tests there. Devproxy is faster.

Claire - Security: if you ask for whitelist, include exact IP and test window. We prefer timeboxed exceptions. Provide a point of contact too.

Nina (DevEx): devproxy quick-run (local):
```
docker run -e RW_API_KEY=sandbox_xxx -p 8080:8080 redwood/devproxy:latest
# then point app at http://localhost:8080
```
Note: local run still egresses from your machine unless you use org-forwarder creds (request via infra).

Taylor W: perfect. last q: any guidance to avoid 429s while ramping? my harness spawns a lot of streams.

Omar - SRE: ramp gradually, honor Retry-After, and use jittered exponential backoff. Cap concurrent streams below the per-key limit. If you need to simulate higher throughput, request a temp quota bump in the infra ticket.

Taylor W: thanks everyone — i'll try devproxy and open an infra ticket if needed. tagging @Nina for follow-up on CI-friendly keys.

Nina (DevEx): ack, will share CI ephemeral key docs. :thumbsup:
